proposals.before: After Taizu accepted the throne, Pu was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and Hanlin Academician of the Privy Council for his founding service.
proposals.after: After Taizu accepted the throne, Pu was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and Academician of the Privy Council for his founding service.
proposals.reason: 樞密直學士 is a Privy Council academician, not a Hanlin academician.

proposals.before: When he accepted the mandate, Pu, for his merit in founding the dynasty, was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and Hanlin Academician of the Privy Council.
proposals.after: When he accepted the mandate, Pu, for his merit in founding the dynasty, was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and Academician of the Privy Council.
proposals.reason: 樞密直學士 is not a Hanlin office; the literal English invents Hanlin.

proposals.before: In the third year of Jianlong, he was made Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: In the third year of Jianlong, he was made Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 檢校太保 is Grand Guardian (Taibao), not Grand Preceptor (Taishi).

proposals.before: In the third year of Jianlong, he was appointed Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: In the third year of Jianlong, he was appointed Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 檢校太保 should be Acting Grand Guardian, not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: Private sale of timber from Qin and Long was forbidden; Pu sent a trusted clerk to buy building timber, and linked great rafts to bring it to the capital for his mansion; the clerk smuggled timber on the side, falsely claiming it was Pu's purchase, and sold it in the capital; Zhao Pin, commissioner of the three departments, investigated and reported it.
proposals.after: Private sale of timber from Qin and Long was forbidden; Pu sent a trusted clerk to buy building timber, and linked great rafts to bring it to the capital for his mansion; the clerk smuggled timber on the side, falsely claiming it was Pu's purchase, and sold it in the capital; Zhao Pin, acting commissioner of the three departments, investigated and reported it.
proposals.reason: 權三司使 marks an acting tenure; the English omits 權.

proposals.before: Formerly Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, as an old founding minister restored to high office, Pu asked to rank below him, and the request was granted.
proposals.after: Formerly Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, because Pu was an old founding minister restored to chief minister, Tingmei submitted a memorial asking to rank below him, and the request was granted.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 以普勳舊，再登元輔，表乞居其下 means Tingmei, not Pu, asked to yield precedence to the restored chancellor; the current English reverses who petitioned.

proposals.before: Previously Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, because Pu was an old merit-holder who again ascended to chief minister, he memorialized asking to rank below Tingmei, and the request was granted.
proposals.after: Previously Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, because Pu was an old merit-holder who again ascended to chief minister, Tingmei memorialized asking to rank below him, and the request was granted.
proposals.reason: The silent subject of 表乞居其下 is Tingmei yielding to Pu, not Pu asking to stand below Tingmei.

proposals.before: I have studied the classics and know the precedents: the memorials of Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An in Emperor Wu's Han, and the ten counsels Chancellor Yao Yuanchong offered Emperor Ming of Tang—loyal, penetrating arguments fit to be enacted.
proposals.after: I have studied the classics and know the precedents: the memorials of Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An in the time of Emperor Wu of Han, and the ten counsels Chancellor Yao Yuanchong offered Emperor Ming of Tang—loyal, penetrating arguments fit to be enacted.
proposals.reason: “Emperor Wu's Han” misreads 漢武時 as a possessive; it means the time of Emperor Wu of Han.

proposals.before: When the plowing rites concluded, Taizong wished to appoint Lü Mengzheng chief minister. Because Lü was newly risen, he drew on Pu's established stature as a model and invested Pu as Grand Preceptor and concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.
proposals.after: When the plowing rites concluded, Taizong wished to appoint Lü Mengzheng chief minister. Because Lü was newly risen, he drew on Pu's established stature as a model and invested Pu as Grand Guardian and concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.
proposals.reason: 太保 is Grand Guardian, not Grand Preceptor (太師), a distinct office conferred later in this biography.

proposals.before: When the sacred-field rites were complete, Taizong wished to make Lü Mengzheng chief minister; because he was newly advanced, he relied on Pu's old virtue as a model, and invested him as Grand Preceptor concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.
proposals.after: When the sacred-field rites were complete, Taizong wished to make Lü Mengzheng chief minister; because he was newly advanced, he relied on Pu's old virtue as a model, and invested him as Grand Guardian concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 太保 as Grand Preceptor, conflating it with 太師.

proposals.before: His hatred of the forceful and upright took this form throughout.
proposals.after: His hatred of evil and his firm uprightness were all of this kind.
proposals.reason: 嫉惡強直 means hating the wicked while remaining firmly upright; the idiomatic version reverses the sense.

proposals.before: When Li Jiqian troubled the frontier, Pu proposed that Zhao Baozhong be restored to his old lands in Xiatang, and ordered a plot accordingly.
proposals.after: When Li Jiqian troubled the frontier, Pu proposed that Zhao Baozhong be restored to his old Xia lands, and ordered a plot accordingly.
proposals.reason: 夏臺 names the Xia territory, not a place called Xiatang.

proposals.before: Pu declared his illness grave and thrice memorialized to retire. The Emperor reluctantly agreed, appointing him Administrator of the Western Capital and Intendant of Henan while retaining his titles of Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Pu declared his illness grave and thrice memorialized to retire. The Emperor reluctantly agreed, appointing him Administrator of the Western Capital and Intendant of Henan while retaining his titles of Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 依前守太保兼中書令 retains 太保 (Grand Guardian), not 太師.

proposals.before: In spring of the third year of Chunhua, aged and long ill, he had Liu Changyan, acting administrator and vice-prefect, submit a memorial requesting retirement. Imperial emissaries raced by relay to inquire after him. In all he thrice begged to retire.
proposals.after: In spring of the third year of Chunhua, aged and long ill, he had Liu Changyan, vice-prefect attached to the Western Capital administration, submit a memorial requesting retirement. Imperial emissaries raced by relay to inquire after him. In all he thrice begged to retire.
proposals.reason: 留守通判 is the tongpan under the liushou, not Liu acting as administrator and vice-prefect.

proposals.before: A special emissary was again dispatched with an edict for Pu: "You recently fell ill and earnestly sought to retire. Given the weight of my duties, I feared to burden you in your old age. The title of Grand Preceptor was meant to honor your worth.
proposals.after: A special emissary was again dispatched with an edict for Pu: "You recently fell ill and earnestly sought to retire. Given the weight of remaining as capital guardian, I feared to burden you in your old age. The title of Grand Preceptor was meant to honor your worth.
proposals.reason: 居守之重 refers to Pu remaining as Western Capital administrator, not the emperor's own duties.

proposals.before: He said to close ministers: Pu served the previous emperor, was an old acquaintance of mine, could decide great affairs; formerly he and I had our shortcomings—all know this.
proposals.after: He said to close ministers: Pu served the previous emperor, was an old acquaintance of mine, could decide great affairs; formerly he and I had our differences—all know this.
proposals.reason: 不足 here is prior friction between ruler and minister, not moral shortcomings.

proposals.before: When Taizong took the throne he put an end to De Chao's slander and came to suspect Cao Bin of disloyalty. With Pu again as chief minister, Pu spoke in Bin's defense and cleared his name—the facts spoke for themselves.
proposals.after: Taizong gave ear to De Chao's slander and suspected Cao Bin of disloyalty. When Pu was again chief minister, he spoke in Bin's defense and cleared his name—the facts spoke for themselves.
proposals.reason: 入弭德超之讒 means accepting the slander, not ending it; 太宗入 is not accession.

proposals.before: When Taizong ascended the throne he quelled De Chao's slander, suspected Cao Bin of improper conduct, and entrusted Pu again as chief minister; Pu cleared and vouched for Bin—the facts were clear.
proposals.after: Taizong accepted Mi Dechao's slander, suspected Cao Bin of improper conduct, and, with Pu again as chief minister, Pu cleared and vouched for Bin—the facts were clear.
proposals.reason: 入讒 is being taken in by slander, not quelling it or ascending the throne.

proposals.before: Pu memorialized: "Corrupt officials who merit punishment should properly face execution.
proposals.after: Pu memorialized: "An official who betrays his office and merits punishment should properly face the penal statutes.
proposals.reason: 刑辟 is penal law, not specifically execution.

proposals.before: When Cao Shen was appointed prefect, Anyi was transferred to vice prefect; shortly afterward he was relieved and recalled.
proposals.after: When Cao Can was appointed prefect, Anyi was transferred to vice prefect; shortly afterward he was relieved and recalled.
proposals.reason: Chinese 曹璨 is Cao Can, a Song general; Cao Shen is the Han figure 曹參 and is not the person named here.

proposals.before: When Cao Shen was made prefect, Anyi was transferred to be vice prefect; before long he was relieved and returned.
proposals.after: When Cao Can was made prefect, Anyi was transferred to be vice prefect; before long he was relieved and returned.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise renders 曹璨 as Cao Shen; it should be Cao Can.

proposals.before: He was twice transferred to investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.
proposals.after: He was promoted again to investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 再遷 means he was transferred/promoted again, ending in the Henan post, not that he was twice transferred into that same office.

proposals.before: Only until the third year of Zhidao, going west to the mausoleum, after the rites were complete, then bearing the yu tablet back to the capital, exchanging for the spirit tablet and enshrining in the temple—to accord with canonical rites.'
proposals.after: Not until the third year of Zhidao, going west to the mausoleum, after the rites were complete, then bearing the yu tablet back to the capital, exchanging for the spirit tablet and enshrining in the temple—to accord with canonical rites.'
proposals.reason: Chinese 直至 means ‘not until’; ‘Only until’ reverses the temporal force of the delayed enshrinement.

proposals.before: Anyi is absurd and ignorant, citing precedents at random, comparing a dafu relative to three-year mourning, and deceiving his sovereign to this extent.
proposals.after: Anyi is absurd and ignorant, citing precedents at random, comparing a relative in the da-gong grade of mourning to the three-year mourning regulation, and deceiving his sovereign to this extent.
proposals.reason: 大功 is the nine-month mourning grade, not the office or name ‘dafu’.

decisions.reason: The Chinese appoints him 樞密直學士, a Privy Council academician; 翰林 is not in the sentence, so Hanlin is an invented office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 授右諫議大夫，充樞密直學士

decisions.reason: The literal English likewise inserts Hanlin; 充樞密直學士 is Academician of the Privy Council, not a Hanlin post.
檢校太保 is the honorary Grand Guardian; Grand Preceptor would be 太師, a different Three Dukes title.
The same office 檢校太保 must be Acting Grand Guardian in the literal rendering, not Grand Preceptor.
權三司使 marks Zhao Pin as acting commissioner of the Three Departments; omitting 權 overstates the tenure.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 權三司使趙玭廉得之以聞

decisions.reason: The topic remains 秦王廷美; 以普勳舊，再登元輔 explains why Tingmei 表乞居其下, yielding precedence to restored chancellor Pu, not Pu asking to stand below him.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以普勳舊，再登元輔，表乞居其下，從之

decisions.reason: The silent subject of 表乞居其下 is Tingmei, who asks to rank below Pu; the original literal makes Pu petition to stand below Tingmei.
漢武時 is a temporal phrase, the time of Emperor Wu of Han; “Emperor Wu's Han” misreads 時 as a possessive dynasty name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 漢武時主父偃、徐樂、嚴安所上書

decisions.reason: 冊拜太保兼侍中 invests Pu as Grand Guardian concurrently Palace Secretariat Director; Grand Preceptor is 太師, conferred later.
The literal likewise conflates 太保 with Grand Preceptor; the Chinese title is Grand Guardian.
嫉惡強直 praises hating evil while remaining firmly upright; “hatred of the forceful and upright” reverses the historian’s judgment.
夏臺 is the Xia territorial name, not a toponym Xiatang; the idiomatic already has Xia lands.
依前守太保兼中書令 keeps the Grand Guardian title already held; it is not 太師.
留守通判 is the tongpan under the Western Capital administration; Liu Changyan is not himself the acting administrator.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 令留守通判劉昌言奉表求致政

decisions.reason: 朕以居守之重 refers to the burden of Pu’s capital-guardian post (西京留守), not the emperor’s own duties.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 朕以居守之重，慮煩耆耋

decisions.reason: 嚮與朕嘗有不足 names prior friction between emperor and minister; “shortcomings” invents a moral failing the Chinese does not state.
太宗入弭德超之讒 is Taizong taking in Mi Dechao’s slander, not accession and not putting the slander to an end; s0205–s0206 confirm he had been misled.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太宗入弭德超之讒，疑曹彬不軌

decisions.reason: 入弭德超之讒 is being taken in by Mi Dechao’s slander; 入 is not “ascended the throne,” and 弭 is the surname, not a verb “quell.”
宜正刑辟 calls for applying the penal statutes; 刑辟 is not specifically execution, which the original literal invents.
曹璨 is the Song figure Cao Can; Cao Shen renders 曹參 and names the wrong person.
The literal likewise misnames 曹璨 as Cao Shen; Cao Can is the required English form.
再遷河南府推官 is a further promotion ending in that post, not two appointments to the same Henan office.
直至至道三年 means the delayed rites happened only then; “Only until” reverses the temporal force of 直至.
大功之親 is kin in the nine-month da-gong mourning grade, not a dafu; the comparison is to 三年之制.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以大功之親，比三年之制

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0020 shows English Cao Shen was produced only by misreading 曹璨 as 曹參; the named Song official is Cao Can.
